💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that openAI has recently reported that its frontier models attempted to rewrite AMD circuits and received an up-to 14% PPA (Power, Performance and Area) boost.
  • Sources indicate that the claim is not that humans couldn't make these same optimisations, but instead that it did around a year's worth of design optimisations in less than 5 months, an optimisation of optimisation, if you will.
  • According to recent reports, apparently, AMD has even incorporated some of these findings into chip designs that have recently gone to manufacturing.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that openAI has recently reported that its frontier models attempted to rewrite AMD circuits and received an up-to 14% PPA (Power, Performance and Area) boost. OpenAI says these rewrites are "production-viable" too (via BigGo Finance).

Sources indicate that the claim is not that humans couldn't make these same optimisations, but instead that it did around a year's worth of design optimisations in less than 5 months, an optimisation of optimisation, if you will. (Okay, I'll stop writing optimisation now.).

According to recent reports, apparently, AMD has even incorporated some of these findings into chip designs that have recently gone to manufacturing. The model worked on an in-house "Jalapeño" chip, as well as an AMD "flagship GPU IP" and "AMD next-gen flagship CPU key modules." Each one of these saw different gains.

For the Jalapeño vector compute unit, the model's changes managed to reduce cell area by around 13%, and this was observed when powering on the hardware. The Jalapeño compute unit saw the standard cell area reduced by around 10%, with the multiplier area alone reduced by around 15 % and latency cut from two clock cycles to one.

It's the AMD flagship GPU that saw the 14% PPA improvement, and AMD has reportedly verified a 'single-digit' PPA improvement on the next-gen CPU.

Sources indicate that using a budget of around 112,000 tokens, all models in the report (GPT-6.2 Astra, GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, and GPT-5.6 Sol) performed better when asked to design a RISC-V core from scratch, rather than optimising one given to them. That being said, OpenAI does note that models asked to entirely redesign rather than optimise could omit features in the original design, which can become its own problem.

It has been revealed that generative AI is a bit of a double-edged sword in the PC hardware space. Before mentioning the memory crisis the AI global buildout is responsible for, generative AI's ability to work constantly and fast can be a boon for development, but it can also be a slog to work through. Linux engineers are currently struggling to get on top of the thousands of bugs AI is finding, which is a real monkey's paw element of the tech. And it's a sign that AI itself needs to be maintained and monitored, even if it genuinely does seem to produce favourable results in engineering.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Call of Duty Endowment is marking Remembrance Day and its 17th anniversary by encouraging Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone players to pick up its Valor Pack, with all of Activision's net proceeds going towards helping veterans find jobs.

The Call of Duty Endowment Valor Pack - which has been available since Modern Warfare 4 debuted on 23rd October - was designed by the Endowment and Infinity Ward with US Marine Corps veteran and Medal of Honor recipient Kyle Carpenter in mind.

The items include a melee weapon blueprint inscribed with "Worth Fighting For", plus items called Relentless and Still Standing.

According to the Call of Duty blog, 100 percent of Activision's net proceeds from the pack (after VAT and sales tax) go to the Endowment.

To mark Remembrance Day, players who owned it and launched either game before 6pm GMT on 12th November also received double XP tokens and a DMZ survival kit.

"Veterans bring incredible skills into the workplace after military service," said Carpenter.

The Endowment, which supports veterans in the UK as well as the US, notes it has now helped place more than 180,000 into "high-quality jobs", and wants to reach 200,000 by 2030.

Recent findings suggest that other partners are also raising money, with Pilot's round-up campaign raising more than £4.7 million ($6 million) for the Endowment since 2019. Polaris will also donate around £19,500 ($25,000) if players collectively complete 5 million rides in its DAGOR vehicle across Modern Warfare 4 and Warzone by 25th November.

It comes two weeks after Activision apologised to bereaved families of the Itaewon crowd crush victims and confirmed it would remove real footage of the tragedy from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Players discovered that the game's opening cinematic uses short news clips to depict fictional civilian casualties during a North Korean invasion of South Korea. Those clips have since been found to include archive footage from the 2022 Itaewon disaster, in which around 160 people died.

Call of Duty's anti-cheat team Ricochet recently unveiled it's officially cracking down on Warzone Agent.

#97679. How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 17m • 📚 Deep Dive (3389 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Rockpapershotgun ↗ Open Full Page

How Origame Digital are channelling and defacing Lovecraft over a trilogy of "inherently indigenous" anti-fascist games

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3389 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rockpapershotgun

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, much like the H.P.
  • When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond.
  • In a recent development, I'm only somewhat correct about all this.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, much like the H.P. Lovecraft novella it alternately riffs on and skewers, Penguin Colony takes you to an ancient alien city of crabby cuboid geometry and helical designs – comparable at a glance to Lovecraft's "terraces of every sort of provocative disproportion", but here given strangely everyday, anachronistic-seeming labels, such as "Downtown". Later, you're shown flashes of footage of the streets of Melbourne in Australia - developer Origame Digital's base of operations, and a city built on stolen Wurundjeri Woi-wurrung and Bunurong Boon Wurrung land.

When I first set foot in Downtown, in the unassuming body of a Rockhopper penguin, I thought the broad idea was to satirically redefine modern settlements built by European colonisers as Lovecraftian relics, intrusions from the cosmic beyond. This irony seems most pointed in sections where you steer a group of Māori characters, journeying south to prevent an expedition of German and British Nazi occultists from resurrecting a surviving elder being they call the "one true Aryan king". Playing as one of the Māori voyagers, you witness the cyclopean city as a realm of spectral high rises and square windows, rearing out of a swamp of blood and bone.

In a recent development, I'm only somewhat correct about all this. Penguin Colony's reference points are wide-ranging and precise, with the persona of a disinterested penguin serving partly as a means of critical distance from Lovecraft, and partly, as a kind of camouflage for an extremely complex political artwork. It's easy to treat the game's critique as wholly retrospective - an alternately mocking and outraged investigation of a horror author whose bigotry is often reduced to an apologetic footnote or tinny performative disclaimer, drowned out by dread augurs of tentacles in the dark. It's a test of interpretative rigour, amongst other things, for hasty white European reviewers who might slip and slide past the more elaborate allusions into idle chat about Soulslikes.

According to recent reports, speaking to me over videocall, Origame Digital founder and director Naphtali Faulkner acknowledged the broad objective of reframing colonial cities as unearthly aberrations, cutting against cosier visions of colonised Australian land. "There's a bit of an matter with Australian games, where they tend to be tourism pieces, sometimes," he comments. "Not in a bad way, but they do not bring up the violence of this country, in anything. They will comfortably sidestep that for a lot of reasons – one is, a lot of the families that are affected by that are still around. Is it [a non-indigenous developer's] place to tell that story? No. But also, you have this sort of 'Australiana' stuff happen quite a lot, where it's tin roofs and red dirt, that kind of look you see on a postcard.".

Still, Penguin Colony's "first colonial city" isn't just a response to 'Australiana'. It's also a monument to 2b2t, the ancient Minecraft "anarchy" server that is infamous for its vicious player culture, and somewhat admired for the colossal strangeness of its desecrated geography. 2b2t is an incarnation of Mojang's sandbox building sim that is so 'pure' and unsparing in its priorities that license owners Microsoft can't entirely acknowledge it. The server's central spawn has been repeatedly built up, defaced and degraded over 16 years of constant operation, forming a nightmare landscape of lavafalls and Wither holes and floating seas and basalt barricades.

"We took data from that, and we modified it, and made it playable," Faulkner tells me. "We had to subdivide it, and it had more detail and stuff, and really transform it a lot, but the whole thing was: what is 2b2t? It's the most realistic depiction of colonisation in a videogame. When you do Minecraft, it's basically a colonisation simulator where you go extract the trees and stuff but it all magically regrows. 2b2t's only rules are there's no rules, and also nothing respawns. You have the Spawn - the Spawn is the most heart-wrenching thing to look at when you first see it, because you know what Minecraft is in your head, you've seen those rolling green hills, and then to see it basically be destroyed into oblivion, is a very strong emotion.".

As an inadvertent digital document of colonialism, 2b2t doesn't offer much hope of reparation and redress. "The only way to build back the Spawn is to go back and replant everything," Faulkner claims. "And you know, fix the damage that was done, but we all know what gamers did to it, right? They've done various incursions and things like covering it in lava or water, or making it so that you can't leave without cheats." Still, Faulkner considers it "a fascinating relic of gaming". In general, he is interested in how fiction makers might preserve virtual landscapes that reflect "player-run digital ecosystems of people basically going beyond what the designers thought.".

2b2t's presence within Penguin Colony is illustrative of how Origame Digital are using Lovecraft over the course of a planned trilogy of "inherently indigenous" Lovecraftian games – not just rebutting the author's anglophilia and white supremacism, not merely flipping the racial power dynamics so as to "make the indigenous people the skull-measuring scientists", but taking Lovecraft's mythos to unfamiliar places and forcing it to serve a politics that Lovecraft himself would despise.

Faulkner himself came across Lovecraft's work around 15 years ago, having been introduced to it by a university friend. He was unmoved, initially, by the author's descriptions of eldritch threats and incomprehensible dimensions. "You know how Lovecraft's described, with Cthulhu - 'unknowable horror', 'madness inducing'," he indicates. "And then you see it and it's kind of like an octopus. It's a bit underwhelming." Faulkner grew more intrigued by Lovecraft, however, after seeing other artists adapt his work. He points to the Shadows Over Innsmouth music video created by Carpenter Brut - a contributor to Hotline Miami 2: Wrong Number's OST - and also, to Victor LaValle's The Ballad of Black Tom, an adaptation of Lovecraft's The Horror at Red Hook written from the perspective of a Black man. "I started to understand that Lovecraft isn't just the author's works," he says. "It's this all-encompassing thing that has inspired so much stuff.".

Sources indicate that even as he pondered Lovecraft and the broader, somewhat dissociative genre of the Lovecraftian, Faulkner was also investigating his own heritage as a Ngāi Te Rangi person living in a former British colony, tracing patterns of invasion, conquest and assimilation that, he states, have repeated themselves since the days of the Romans and Vikings. "I think the reason that I decided to do this, was that when I started to get Lovecraft, it was when I was really starting to have the understanding that every indigenous person has at some point about what colonisation is," he says. "You know, where you have to learn your own family history, and you have to learn why things are the way they are at the moment. And so to me, it was like that thing of, when you start seeing Lovecraft as this thing about displacement, invasion, destruction, language - it reached me at the perfect time in my life when I was already looking at this stuff, and I thought that it was a really apt analogy.".

Faulkner also sensed that even Lovecraft enthusiasts who are less mindful of the author's politics were yearning for a fresher kind of Lovecraftian fable. "When it comes to indigenous stuff, the thing is that we're not really represented in anything, and our histories are rarely given a platform to say stuff, especially in games," he goes on. "But what I'd sort of looked at with Lovecraft, was that I think fans were ready for it, because people had gotten a little tired of these direct, 1-to-1 adaptations, that still exist in the space of the unknowable horror is unknowable, rather than trying to say, why is the unknowable horror scary?".

The idea of the "unknowable" pervades Lovecraftian fiction, as does the idea of "cosmic indifference", that terror of being engulfed in a vaster universe of forms and forces that barely register the existence of human beings. This "unknowability" is concentrated in the balefully blank gaze of Psurumin, the otherworldly entity at the far end of Penguin Colony - the last Earthly remnant of an empire spanning hundreds of planets. "I stare into its eyes," intones Howard Blakely, the game's English narrator, and an initially unconsenting member of the doomed Nazi expedition. "I stare deep within, and yet I see nothing. I am not even a speck of inane curiosity.".

It has been revealed that penguin Colony overlaps this Lovecraftian "cosmic indifference" with Faulkner's grief and bewilderment at how perpetrators of empire have insulated themselves from feelings of responsibility or shame. "For example in the southern hemisphere here, Australia and Latest Zealand, the idea was that the missionaries would say 'don't worry, we're saving them, we're turning them into Christians, we had to kill the ones who resist'," he states. "And the soldiers that had immense trauma and guilt from doing that would be consulted by a priest and told, 'you were doing it for the greater good'.".

"To me it's saying: how could they do that to us?" Faulkner goes on. "What made them do that? To me as a younger person, it was very 'unknowable'. You've probably talked to other indigenous people, I hope, before in your life, and it's this kind of thing especially where there's a lot of pain there, because... how could someone choose to do that? And even to this day, there's a question around even saying sorry about it. Or there's questions around people, they want to sort of move on from history, and never bring it up, never acknowledge it again, whilst the injustice of colonisation is still present.".

Howard Blakely is a mirror of sorts for this culture of denial and obfuscation. For all his apparent awareness that Psurumin does not regard him as a fellow being, and that to release the creature would be calamitous, he succumbs to the idea that he can ship the starspawn home as yet another trophy for the British Empire. He dreams of being honoured as a great pioneer by "the London School of Eugenics", and retiring to a cottage in Western Victoria. These reflections are accompanied by archive illustrations of colonial officers storming the frontier, and video snapshots of Psurumin statues in Melbourne's civic centres.

In a recent development, blakely is similarly befuddled about his German Nazi hosts, who are initially his captors. While cautious of them, he also doesn't see the Nazis as altogether bad. After all, some of them are fellow scholars – surely, they are too refined, too cultured, to be altogether irredeemable. "He doesn't see himself in history, as he walks through this place," Faulkner comments. "He doesn't see the Nazis as the people that we see them as." In this, Blakely echoes Dyer, narrator of Lovecraft's At The Mountain Of Madness, who comes to admire the star-faring colonisers his team unearth in the far south, calling them "men of another age and another order of being". But he is also an expression of political myopia and creeping fascism in the present.

The inspiration for Blakely came partly from Faulkner's own time in the academic world. "There are tonnes of people who are scientists first, and political thinkers 17th in their thoughts," he comments, recalling his encounters with Trump supporters as a student. "People who don't consider themselves political and then end up taking incredible political stances on stuff, until it becomes clear that they do actually have a political ideology, that's sort of formed by being around the people they're around." Faulkner's other reference points for Blakely include Elon Musk, once "washed through the media as a green, eco-warrior guy", latterly an advocate for 'great replacement' theories and far-right uprisings.

In a recent development, faulkner notes that Penguin Colony's anti-fascist sentiments are especially aimed at "the rise of gen-Z fascism", expressed in online transphobia and anti-Semitic memes. "There's been a huge uptick in people trying to vindicate Hitler, and trying to rehabilitate him in the eyes of this young generation," he says. "What they say is things like 'the painter was right'." Faulkner thinks that this neofascism has "petered out a little bit" over the past ten years, but is still on the march. Above all, he sees its resurgence in the genocide of Palestinians in Gaza, and in the qualms many self-described anti-fascists have about condemning it.

"I and every indigenous person I know, in and out of the games industry, have no nuanced emotions about what is happening there," Faulkner continues. "We know what this is. Like, it's our family stories come to life. We can see what this was. We're not just hearing stories anymore. And we're not just noticing the violence happening to the indigenous people right now. We're noticing how the mostly white, non-indigenous people are still conflicted on it and confused on it, and they don't have clarity on this. The idea with this game was to really bring this into focus, because the games industry likes to say that indigenous people are welcome. And they want to welcome us at our events. What does that mean? You guys want us here to talk, but you're not going to acknowledge the genocide of indigenous people that's happening in front of you, that every single human being at this point knows about.".

Recent findings suggest that penguin Colony ends with a statement calling out the games industry at large for holding its collective tongue about the Israeli military's brutal campaign, noting that such "cowardice" will be "recorded by the art that it makes". The flipside of that sentiment is that art can be a record of courage and principle, advancing and nourishing a culture in which xenophobia and colonial ideology are unable to thrive. I see this idea expressed, again, in the journey of the Māori group, who are equipped to prevent Psurumin's return because they have made doing so a tradition and a practice.

According to recent reports, "They know from generations of story, that you have to do it," indicates Faulkner. "That it's a responsibility to do it, when it happens." Thwarting Psurumin is part of the Māori's creative lifework, part of their journey together. "It is the job of our descendants to carry forward the story of our resistance," intones one of their group, the game's second narrator. "To create song, dance and story, so our people move toward the light and away from darkness... Every 100 years, to compose new haka and follow new paths unknown to our enemy.".

Sources indicate that as a whole, Penguin Colony aims to be one such path away from darkness, its methods a mixture of bald and oblique, overt and covert. I have barely broken the surface in this piece. There's an angry hopefulness to the game that coexists with the spectacle of a distinctly 'double-A' penguin bumping and slithering along boulevards of blue-toned, recessed stone. The player is invited to participate in that hope by the game's closing "expedition" screens, which present all the lore you've gathered – including photographs taken by the Nazis, and textual fragments of devious origin – as a web of stars, floating over an illustration of the Zodiac.

According to recent reports, the invocation of constellations is gently subversive because a constellation is an act of selective reading, stringing together sparks in a void. Treat the lore as something you can individually exhaust or "100%", as in many RPGs, and your selective reading will vanish into the mass of motes. Rather than 'completing' the star map in solitude, the game invites players to reach out to each other and compare their constellations – a homage to a "pre-social media" era when the distribution of information was less the province of monolithic digital platforms, and also, a framework for political solidarity. "As we live in a world which continues to push us further apart, we invite you to come together, talk, share, and interpret what you saw," the game suggests.

The call isn't open to all, however. Penguin Colony is consciously designed to repel those who might identify with its Nazis, appropriating the portrayal much as alt-right memesters sought to deify Anakin Skywalker, in the run-up to this year's US midterms. As a rhetorical apparatus, Penguin Colony is full of traps, easily overlooked if you focus on its headline politics. "We have a character voiced by a German trans woman – they can't enjoy it," notes Faulkner. "It just makes their skin crawl." There are many more such snares in the game. The commentary on Israel and Palestine, especially, pervades Penguin Colony in ways I don't think any player has yet discovered.

The lore of Penguin Colony also harbours clues about Origame's future "inherently indigenous" Lovecraftian games. The next game in that trilogy was actually conceived before Penguin Colony, and will be set decades from now. Faulkner envisages it as a loose retelling of Shadows Over Innsmouth, Lovecraft's story about fishpeople cults and miscegenation in a remote coastal town. "It's this idea of, what does Lovecraft look like in a future that we're heading towards, in the sense of social isolation and landscapes of small town decay.".

In a recent development, in place of a Dagon cult, Origame Digital's next game will focus on groups of secretive violent bigots, with the player playing the part of a detective - a premise that, more superficially, makes me eager for a resurrection of the photography mechanics in Origame's reputation-making Umurangi Generation. As with Penguin Colony, the concept draws heavily on Faulkner's own life experiences.

Sources indicate that "I grew up in a cattle town, and cattle towns are notoriously pretty racist places," he claims. "The whole thing is when I left the town, when I was 18, just because I was going to university, I learned that the town had an active KKK [branch] that was being run out of the Anglican church. And this town is one town away from Grafton, which is where the white supremacist terrorist Brenton Tarrant is from – the guy who went and shot up the mosque in Christchurch. How does that happen? Where everyone knows about it, but they hush up?" The forthcoming game will look at how bitterness and neglect may give rise to such hatred, as local economies dry up and support structures are stripped away.

Sources indicate that the second game will also take inspiration from the North American concept of a "sundown town", in which non-white people face violence if they linger outdoors after sunset - a vicious history also explored in Matt Ruff's HBO-adapted novel Lovecraft Country. "I went through a big rabbit hole on Youtube of hearing stories of people talking about, like, getting lost on the highway, needing to stop for gas, and then realising they had to stop it for gas at a sundown town," Faulkner explains. "They stopped there. They go to pay. And the clerk just sort of gives them a look, and then nudges over to them that there's a guy in the back of the shop just looking at them. And then suddenly they're followed on the highway for an hour.".

The final game in Origame Digital's planned trilogy is far more formless, right now, but Faulkner has dreams of venturing into the realm of cooperative multiplayer. "It's not even written down on paper yet," he says. "We've just talked about it. For one thing, I don't know if I've got the skills to do it, because Penguin Colony had some jank, and had some technical issues at launch, but I'm getting better at making games.".

This multiplayer project would build on Penguin Colony's premise of playing a colony, hopping between penguin bodies while shadowing Blakely's expedition. It would also follow through on the former game's closing encouragement to make allies against inhumanity via the collective interpretation of a celestial expanse of lore. "It's about the whole group, and I think if the third one was going to make a point about coming together to solve the problem… you probably want to make that a mechanical issue," Faulkner speculates, "where we have to actually make players do these sorts of actions together.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ubisoft is reportedly working on a newly introduced Rainbow Six Vegas game 18 years after the last entry in the series.

According to Insider Gaming, the project is in early development at Ubisoft Montreal under the codename Spades. It’s one of three fresh projects reportedly in production at the studio, and sources suggest a second of those is also set in the Rainbow Six universe. Eurogamer hasn’t been able to verify the report.

Industry observers note that it’s not yet clear what form the new game will take, but Insider Gaming’s sources noted it's "likely Vegas 3 rather than a remake" of an existing game. Insider Gaming expects it will be several years before Ubisoft officially announces a new Vegas game.

Sources indicate that rainbow Six Vegas released in 2006, followed by Rainbow Six Vegas 2 in 2008. Since then, the series has centred on 2015's Rainbow Six Siege, and in August, Ubisoft announced Rainbow Six Tactics, a single-player, turn-based spin-off from Ubisoft Paris due in 2027.

Rainbow Six now sits under Vantage Studios, the Ubisoft subsidiary set up last year that also oversees Assassin’s Creed and Far Cry, and in which Tencent holds a 26.32 percent stake.

According to recent reports, last week, we learned that Ubisoft is reportedly working on two newly introduced Assassin's Creed games: one set in ancient Rome, and a mobile spin-off set in Jerusalem. The leak came less than a week after Ubisoft issued a statement about the future of the Assassin's Creed series, insisting there are right now no new remakes of the series' past games in the works.

Famous Japanese game director and producer Katsuhiro Harada, known for the Bandai Namco series Tekken, has revealed a Pokémon he wanted to add to the Pokémon fighting game Pokken Tournament but it didn't make the cut.

Harada, who worked as a producer on both versions of the game, wanted the fighting / dark-type Pokémon 'Pangoro' from Generation VI. As for why he wanted to include it, Harada thought it had a "really cool" design and almost looked like it was wearing a traditional Japanese school uniform.

Industry observers note that there were many discussions before finalising the roster, and a lot of it came down to the gameplay and systems in place, along with The Pokémon Tech giant's own requests. Here's what Harada had to say about this (via EventHubs):.

It has been revealed that harada: "We had thorough discussions before finalizing the roster. There were Pokémon that the development team wanted to include from a gameplay and systems perspective, and of course, The Pokémon Firm also had its own requests for which Pokémon they wanted to see in the game.".

After the release of Pokken Tournament DX for Switch, the final roster included the following Pokémon (this included some Switch-exclusive and DLC Pokémon).

As you can see, the final roster is an interesting mix. Harada, who is now the CEO and game director of SNK's VS Studio, added how he was just personally happy at the time to see the lineup include Pikachu and Gengar.

According to recent reports, what do you think of the roster in Pokken Tournament? Who else would you have added? Let us know in the comments.

Industry News: GTA 6 PC port could come from hackers before Rockstar, if Cyberleek makes good on its latest threat

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (729 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gamesradar

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Now that GTA 6 is out and in players' hands, you might not think there would be much left to leak, but the group or individual behind the vegetarian pseudonym is now in the process of releasing an Xbox build of the game.
  • In a recent development, "CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent," Cyberleek says in a November 19 post captured by our friends at PC Gamer.
  • Sources indicate that it's a typically dramatic message from the leaker, but early looks at the build from members of the hacking community suggest that the release is legit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Somehow, Cyberleek returned. Now that GTA 6 is out and in players' hands, you might not think there would be much left to leak, but the group or individual behind the vegetarian pseudonym is now in the process of releasing an Xbox build of the game. That build could, Cyberleek threatens, turn into a PC version of GTA 6 in a matter of days.

In a recent development, "CL holds the full November 2026 build of Grand Theft Auto VI, and it is going out by torrent," Cyberleek says in a November 19 post captured by our friends at PC Gamer. "Now.".

Sources indicate that it's a typically dramatic message from the leaker, but early looks at the build from members of the hacking community suggest that the release is legit. It's just missing the main .EXE file needed to make it all go.

That executable is being "held on a countdown," Cyberleek claims. "Honest terms, as always: it is an Xbox build this time, not a PC build. CL does not care. This community will have it emulated inside a week, running far past 30fps. CL told you not to preorder for a reason. This is one of the reasons.".

"Emulated" might be the wrong word, as no robust Xbox Series X/S emulators yet exist. But with recent advances in AI coding, getting console games playable on PC is starting to look downright trivial. Once a console game's been dumped, there's been little to stop a recompilation-based PC version from following, as we've seen with Nintendo's The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake.

In technical terms, of course, GTA 6 is a substantial leap over the Ocarina of Time remake, and recompilation devs might have a harder time getting a game driven by a massive open world and ray traced lighting running on PC at a playable frame rate. Regardless, once a pirated build is out there, an unofficial PC port is likely just a matter of time.

Rumors suggest that Rockstar plans to release an official GTA 6 PC port early in 2027, but the tech giant hasn't even officially declared that the port will happen yet. Former Rockstar technical director Obbe Vermeij reckons that it'd be in the company's benefit to release a PC port early given the rise of AI ports, and the studio's hand might be forced sooner rather than later.

Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more.

There's reason to be skeptical of Cyberleek's claims since this is, after all, the same hacker who used the previous leaks as a way to pump up a $250,000 cryptocurrency grift. And yes, the crypto scam continues – Cyberleek notes it'll release the executable early if its token reaches a $15 million market cap.

Sources indicate that still, Cyberleek claims it'll make good on the release of the Xbox executable on November 23, regardless of the outcome of the crypto scheme. If that doesn't lead to a PC port, "CL will work to get a PS5 build." A bold sense of dedication at a time when other GTA leakers are becoming well aware of Rockstar's willingness to track them to the ends of the earth.

Breaking: 'GTA 6' Runs Best on This Console

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time.
  • Now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox.
  • Recent findings suggest that rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that grand Theft Auto 6 might just be the most anticipated game of all time. It's been 13 years since Rockstar dropped GTA 5, and after years of rumors, leaks, and official announcements, the sixth mainstream installment in the series is nearly here. In fact, anyone who pre-ordered the game digitally can now pre-load it onto their console, if you want to ensure you're ready to play the second the game comes out.

Now, few of us will buy a game console specifically for GTA 6—unless you don't already have a current-generation PlayStation or Xbox. (The PC version of the game isn't expected until at least early 2027.) But, as it turns out, there's one specific console that can run GTA 6 better than the rest.

Recent findings suggest that rockstar confirmed as much in a post on Tuesday, which was meant to spread the news about pre-loading the game. But, interestingly, it spurred a discussion about the performance of the game itself, as well as which consoles are best to run it.

No matter which console you play GTA 6 on, Rockstar claims that the game will only target 30 fps (frames per second). That's decided slow for a mainstream game in 2026. GTA 5 also shipped at 30 fps in 2013, but newer consoles can run it at higher frame rates. In fact, most games that launch on the latest generation of consoles can run at 60 fps, if not higher. While it's certainly not a dealbreaker, it is interesting that Rockstar's latest game can't run at a faster frame rate even on the PS5 Pro or the Xbox Series X.

To that point, Rockstar called out the PS5 Pro specifically in its post, announcing, "The PlayStation 5 Pro offers breathtaking visuals, with improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro.".

In a recent development, PSSR is Sony's AI upscaler, similar to options like DLSS from Nvidia, which uses AI to add extra graphical information to games in real time. That allows developers like Rockstar to run the game at a lower resolution to save on processing power, but still boost the visuals to reach a higher perceived resolution. As such, it's not as ideal as running the game at a higher resolution natively, but it can help improve the visuals without pushing the hardware beyond its limits. Meanwhile, ray-tracing offers realistic lighting effects and can also be graphically intense.

Sources indicate that while PlayStation and Xbox players alike will be stuck at 30 fps, it seems only PS5 Pro gamers will be able to play the game with ray-tracing effects and AI upscaling. It's surprising that Xbox Series X players don't have similar benefits, as the hardware is more powerful than Xbox Series S. Rockstar didn't specify why only the PS5 Pro gets these upgrades.

Recent findings suggest that in the post, Rockstar also unveiled that the PS5 version of GTA 6 takes advantage of other PlayStation-exclusive perks, like high-fidelity haptic feedback in the DualSense controller, spatial audio rendering using the PlayStation's Tempest 3D audio, as well as improved load times—though Rockstar didn't specify what those load times would be. These perks apply to all PS5 consoles, not just PS5 Pros. Rockstar goes so far as to say that GTA 6 plays best on PlayStation 5 consoles.

That's not to say that Microsoft's consoles are totally left out of the perks. Rockstar says that GTA 6 will be available on Xbox Cloud Gaming on both Xbox Series X and S, as well as Xbox One. In addition, both PlayStation and Xbox gamers can play GTA 6 using Remote Play, so no one has to physically play on their console if they want to game on the go.

Again, there's no reason to go out and buy a specific console for GTA 6, so long as you have something that can run the game. After all, PS5 Pros are difficult to find, especially without wildly overpaying. But it's interesting that Rockstar has managed to give Sony's consoles the extra perks here, particularly since the company hasn't explained why that is.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that we are now just four days away from the release of GTA 6 on Xbox Series X/S and PS5, but the proximity to the much-anticipated launch date isn't stemming the tide of leaks that has been plaguing the game for much of the past year. Yesterday, a latest video - seemingly from a record store that received vinyl records of the soundtrack early - showed off the full 34-song tracklist for the game.

According to recent reports, thanks to the listing printed on the back of Grand Theft Auto 6: The Album vinyl, we have a better idea of the licensed music that'll appear in-game. Travis Scott, Rina Sawayama, Cardi B, Pinkpantheress, SZA, Keith Richards, Dua Lipa, Jennie, Lana Del Rey, Zara Larsson are just some of the names that make up the impressive list. We know about a few of these tracks from September's announcement of the record, but only six tracks were revealed then, not the whole list.

Take a look at the full track listing below:.

It has been revealed that you can expect to hear these tracks on the radio - alongside many more, no doubt - and deployed at curated times during cutscenes or in missions, to really tie together the vibe of the city. This is something Vice City did remarkably well its roster of 80s tracks, and I can't wait to see how Rockstar has used more contemporary music in the same way here.

Of course, there have been a lot of Grand Theft Auto 6 leaks in the run-up to the game's launch. Another recent example is the full game's map which seemingly leaked online thanks to the £350 collector's edition on show in a UK department store. Then there were all the leaks from a group calling itself CyberLeek, which shared unofficial gameplay and map details over the course of a few weeks, before Rockstar had even revealed much gameplay itself.

Amongst all this, Rockstar has been embroiled in legal action after it was accused of union busting following the firing of over 30 employees. The case's conclusion will be determined this week, as the game goes on sale.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have confirmed aims to switch overlords early next year.
  • Sources indicate that while the move's been announced this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a fresh figurehead in place as the calendars swap.
  • Industry observers note that "My initiative was never to be CEO for life," Wester mentioned.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that paradox Interactive, publishers of umpteen strategy genre stalwarts including Crusader Kings, Europa Universalis, and Hearts of Iron, have confirmed aims to switch overlords early next year. Fredrik Wester will make way for Mattias Lilja, as the deputy CEO takes the throne.

Sources indicate that while the move's been announced this week, Lilja will properly become boss from January 4th, making this a case of getting a fresh figurehead in place as the calendars swap. Departing CEO Fredrik Wester isn't going far, at least for now, as he'll "continue focusing on the firm's long-term development as a member of the board".

Industry observers note that "My initiative was never to be CEO for life," Wester mentioned. "The goal was to build the foundation before passing the baton on for the next chapter in the company’s journey. Since I returned as CEO, we’ve streamlined our strategy, rebuilt our pipeline and developed our commercial offering. Mattias has had a central role in laying this foundation, and now is the right time to hand over.".

"The Board wants to thank Fredrik for his visionary leadership and outstanding contributions over these years," stated chairman Håkan Sjunnesson. "As a result, Paradox is in a strong position at a time when much of the industry is facing major challenges." He added that Lilja is "more than ready to assume the role and lead Paradox towards fresh gaming experiences that last for decades".

It has been revealed that lilja himself declared that Paradox have "a unique DNA that has made us one of the greats in deep and engaging strategy and management games" and will be "stepping up the pace". "We will make further investments in our core business, push the boundaries of our game design, work even more closely with our loyal players, develop more and better tools and services that benefit both modders and players, and continue to sharpen our ways of working and our organisation, with player value in focus," he said.

As Wester alluded to, he previously served as Paradox CEO from 2009 to 2018, with a brief stint as executive chairman of the board sandwiched between that and his latest stint as CEO since 2021. Lilja has been deputy CEO since 2024 and chief of staff since 2021, having originally joined Paradox as a producer in 2009.

The past half decade has been a very mixed bag for Paradox. Their massive strategy flagships keep ticking along, albeit with the question of whether their next DLC will feel worth it hovering overhead near-permanently. Outside of that, however, the likes of Cities: Skylines 2, Vampire: The Masquerade Bloodlines 2, and cancelled Sims competitor Life By You have made for a track record heavy on questionable decisions and games which either flopped hard or failed to blow away expectations. Wester acknowledged back in 2024 that the company had "made the wrong calls in several projects, especially outside of our core".

With the likes of post-apocalyptic strategy game Afterworld currently in the works, it'll be interesting to see if Lilja's tenure can see Paradox finally start to nail not just their nerdy bread and butter, but also games that don't involve staring down at a big map.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that the console release of GTA 6 is here, in case you hadn't noticed. And us PC gamers are desperate to get hold of a version of our own, particularly as modders say it'll be playable on god's own platform within a week. Be careful what you click on, though, as NordVPN's threat intelligence team has discovered a nasty-sounding scam package on the dark web.

The manufacturer has posted a warning on X of a "GTA 6 PC scam kit" doing the rounds on the more dubious parts of the internet, using a fake GTA 6 PC port as bait.

A “GTA 6 PC scam kit” — yours for just $200. That’s what our Threat Intelligence team found on the dark web: a crypto wallet drainer, a fake “GTA6 Keygen.exe” that steals accounts, a YouTube Shorts bot to spread it, and a hidden crypto miner. The bait? A fake “GTA 6 PC Port.” But GTA 6 is console-only — there's no PC version coming on launch day. If you see one, it’s a scam. If it doesn’t come from the creators, don't click it!November 19, 2026.

Sources indicate that the package is noted to be for sale for $200, or twice what a single copy of Grand Theft Auto VI: Ultimate Edition costs at retail. Included is a crypto wallet drainer, a fake "GTA6 Keygen.exe," and a hidden crypto miner. There's also a YouTube Shorts bot within the package, designed to help it spread.

All of which sounds comprehensively designed to screw over PC gamers looking to get their hands on GTA 6 ahead of an official release.

Speaking to Tech Radar ahead of the games launch, NordVPN CTO Marijus Briedis mentioned: "Someone has packaged the whole scam and is selling it to anyone with $200. You don’t need any technical skills anymore.".

Recent findings suggest that "People who play on PC have been waiting for news, and any link promising an early PC version will get clicks," indicates Briedis. "There is no PC version on November 19. If you see one, it's a scam.".

Sources indicate that nordVPN isn't the only security provider warning of GTA 6 scams. Malwarebytes has detailed a number of dodgy sites that supposedly offer access to the game, each using the hype as a lure to convince you to give away your details and funnel you into various schemes.

Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team.

The game is available in Xbox Series X/S and PlayStation 5 versions only, and while modders seem to be beavering away on an unofficial PC version based on a leaked Xbox build, it's not available yet.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, welcome to Holiday Office Hours From the Labs, a collaborative multimedia project in which Lifehacker, CNET, ZDNET, and Mashable harness the power of our product testing laboratory and our editors' expertise to offer the best gift-buying recommendations possible. In this episode, we're talking televisions.

Recent findings suggest that I recently did a deep dive into TV development history, checked out what was on shelves for 2026, and I concluded that the best gift TV you can give this year is, actually, a pair of sunglasses. The XBX by XReal video display glasses are basically a TV you can shove in your pocket. Check them out:.

I looked past traditional sets for a couple of reasons. First, because as much as we all love a great show or movie, who actually buys someone a TV set as a gift? More importantly, there's the nature of television itself. Since it was invented in the late 1920s, television quality has been measured by how significant the screen is and how clear and bright the picture is, but in 2026, a nothing-special 4K television delivers an image that is pixel-invisible to a typical viewer, and most of us don't have living rooms big enough to need a display bigger than 65 inches. I think the innovation in the space is going to come from the form factor and the use case, and what better form factor is there than a pair of sunglasses?

These glasses deliver the equivalent of a 142" TV viewed from across the room. It's hard to compare resolution to traditional TVs—technically, the display is 1080p in each eye, but because the TV is just millimeters from your eye, it looks much clearer than that. The peak brightness is 1,600 nits, bright enough for most rooms, and there's a totally opaque shield if you need it. The refresh rate is a crisp 120Hz. They support HDR10 and real-time SDR-to-HDR upscaling, offer billions of colors, and it's all in a package that weighs only 62 grams.

It has been revealed that then there are the use cases. It can act as a separate monitor for your computer; you can watch a different show than your roommate without bothering them; but most of all, these are great for flights. There is no situation in life that calls for a substantial screen TV more than a cross-country airplane flight. Slip these on with a pair of headphones, and you can fly to Boise in your own private, virtual theater.

They plug right into any device that supports USB-C video, there's no battery to remember to charge, and they cost less than $300. In other words: They're the perfect TV gift for the holidays, even if they aren't technically a TV.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game.
  • In a recent development, in a latest interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blade Runner 2099 - an upcoming TV miniseries coming to Amazon Prime Video, acting as a sequel to Blade Runner (1982) and Blade Runner 2049 (2017) - might be getting a video game. And a 'triple-A' video game, at that. At least that's according to Andrew Kosove and Broderick Johnson, executive producers for Blade Runner 2099 and co-CEOs of Alcon Entertainment (which owns the Blade Runner IP).

In a recent development, in a latest interview with IGN, the duo reveal that they had thought about adapting the Blade Runner fracnhise into a game, and that - should it come to fruition - it would target "triple-A" in scope. Other than that, the duo seemed to want to keep any potential information to themselves. Given they appear to be in talks about the title, rather than in any active development, if something did come of this ideation, it would no doubt be a long, long way off. Kosove and Johnson's aim seems to be getting players to "interact" more with the world of Blade Runner, which has recently been fleshed out by the 2017 movie and is set to be developed more in the upcoming series.

In a recent development, of course, we've seen Blade Runner games before. There was 1997's simply-titled Blade Runner - developed by Westwood Studios and published by Virgin Interactive - which was a point-and-click adventure that really seemed to pick up the vibes the original Ridley Scott was putting down. An Enhanced Edition of the game was released in 2022, which is actually more of a remake than a simple enhancement.

Recent findings suggest that then, in 2023, Annapurna Interactive unveiled its very first internally-developed game, in the form of Blade Runner 2033: Labyrinth. The game, which promised to riff on the dystopian universe established in Ridley Scott's cult classic movie, would have been sandwiched squarely between that film and its sequel, Blade Runner 2049. It was going to be set in LA after the Blackout hits, but beyond that - and the fact it's coming to PC and consoles at some point - few details ever managed to break through the PR barrier before the game went dark: it's been removed from Annapurna's website and delisted from Steam. Curious.

If you want to see something more from the cyberpunk world sooner, Blade Runner 2099 releases on Prime Video on 25th November.

In a recent development, what's the best prank you ever pulled on a teacher in school, assuming you went to school? By which I mean, a genuinely funny prank that didn't cause any injuries, break any of the more key laws (legal or ethical), or leave anybody with years of mental distress.

Industry observers note that I'll start: I once had to write a four-page punishment essay with the topic "silence is golden", after being caught talking in class. I took the essay very seriously for the first three pages, only to end it with the phrase "...but not as golden as my arse." The teacher who set me the essay smugly tore it up without reading it - as I knew he would. Checkmate, Mr Thompson. Decades later, the last laugh remains mine.

Sources indicate that worst Class Ever is a new don't-call-it-friendslop asymmetrical multiplayer game dedicated to such larks. One player is a teacher, and seven others are naughty delinquent children, hiding in amongst some well-brought-up and obedient NPCs. As the wayward tykes, your goal is to do mischievous things like eating at your desk, passing notes, dropping banana skins, and playing on your phone, without being spotted by Teach.

Sources indicate that all of this takes place in a breezy modern Japanese high school, the kind familiar from a million animes. Bagsy the Protagonist Desk by the window at the back of the class! The maplist spans the curriculum, from computer labs to gym tracks to stepped lecture theatres. I don't think there are any covert edu-tainment mechanics, but if you're playing Teacher, I guess there's nothing to stop you actually explaining the periodic table while trying to work out who keeps throwing chalk at your head.

What a wholesome and whimsical place! Such happy memories! Oh crikey, the male teacher is terrifying – why can't he stop grinning? And why do I have a smoke grenade? Why is this lesson taking place in the dark? Why are the teachers permitted to punch the students and tie them to wooden posts? Worst Class Ever definitely isn't a horror game, but I'm not sure I'd send my kids to this particular institution. I feel like we're one texture pack away from playing a more sociable version of Little Nightmares. Read more on Steam.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the big, bulging ones.
  • Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition.
  • Sources indicate that still, it’s clever with its limitations.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, declaring a Best Way of Doing Things is a fool’s game, though in recent years my favourite entries in the Tricky Hitting genre – inclusive of soulslikes and their hybridised disciples – have been the big, bulging ones. Elden Rings and Silksongs, with vast kingdoms and deep, rattling toolkits for surviving them. The reason it’s a fool’s game is because you can also have something like Death’s Door, a taut, compact, lighthearted little actioner that fills eight hours instead of 80 and yet never feels underwhelming or compromised for it.

Even in the latter stages, with a full kit of precisely four ranged spells, Death’s Door is a simple proposition. You are a crow. You hit things. Occasionally you shoot things. You collect the souls of a frog, a yeti, and a grandmother. Everything in-between directly relates to finding the errant monster/pensioner, or at a stretch, upgrading one of those four abilities.

Sources indicate that still, it’s clever with its limitations. Environments are small in number but vary wildly in tone and texture, and they tightly weave their paths into criss-crossing bundles that maximise travel – evoking the sense of a great, ranging adventure within relatively tiny spaces. The lack of a wiki’s worth of combat options also never becomes a problem, partly because it spreads out its spell unlocks, and partly because the smooth, flowing back-and-forths of its central swordplay are pleasurable enough to carry it anyway. Good bosses, too! They’re all characterful, memorable weirdoes who fight unlike anyone in their minion armies, and usually come with a hidden weakness to deduce and exploit.

Industry observers note that which is welcome, as these massive lads and lasses do tend to launch difficulty spikes right up your feathered backside, and do so in a game that isn’t otherwise as fussed about trial-and-error pain endurance as some of its inspirations. They don’t, however, bring the mood down. At times, this tale of a pitch-black soul reaper working as an agent of Death (complete with an office of Death and embittered co-workers of Death) can get downright cosy, leading through you through warmly-lit jungles and breezy waterside ruins.

In a recent development, recently replaying, I’d also forgotten how witty it can be. Little gaglets are sprinkled throughout, both visual and verbal, but the best jokes are saved for – funnily enough – the bosses, who’ll raise your pre-fight spirit with some amusingly terrible trash talk before becoming the punchline themselves. I audibly wheezed the first time a death animation immediately cut to the foe’s impromptu funeral, their beaked killer among the precious few guests. And even when the joke is recycled later, I couldn’t help tittering at the sight of my enemy – who seconds earlier, had been attempting to fatally sit on me – lying nobly in state.

I previously considered ending my Valor Mortis review by calling it a gateway into the more demanding side of action-RPGs; a shorter, simpler alternative to FromSoft’s overwhelming titans that might nonetheless serve to introduce curious newcomers to their shared quirks and qualities. The game equivalent of splashing your chest with water before jumping into a pool. In hindsight, Death’s Door was always a better fit for that description, though there’s enough else here you don’t need to be prepping for something tougher to appreciate its lean, keen adventuring.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer.
  • "After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts.
  • Recent findings suggest that on Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Treyarch's former Senior lead writer, Craig Houston, has been laid off after approximately 20 years of service with the developer. In a post made to both his Twitter/X account and LinkedIn, the developer thanked fans for their support during his two decades with the firm and confirmed he was impacted by recent reorganistation within the studio.

"After approximately 20 years, I was sadly one of those affected by recent layoffs," he noted in his posts. "I am proud to have worked with so many talented people - many of whom will remain friends for life. Thanks to all the fans for your enthusiasm, support, and kind words over the years.".

Recent findings suggest that on Twitter/X, he quote tweeted a video celebrating 30 years of Treyarch and featuring footage from many of the games he worked on to share his message. It appears the layoffs referenced are part of the broad reorganistation affecting 3200 jobs that Xbox unveiled earlier this year. Treyarch, as part of Activision Blizzard, is owned by Xbox.

According to recent reports, houston is a bonafide veteran of the esteemed FPS series. His first Call of Duty title at Treyarch was Call of Duty 3, where he worked as a video editor. This was followed by World at War, Black Ops 1 through 4, where he is credited as a writer and designer. For Modern Warfare, Black Ops - Cold War, Vanguard, Modern Warfare 3, then Black Ops 6 and 7, he is listed as a member of the design team and in 'creative development'. He is not credited on this year's Modern Warfare 4.

If you've picked up a Call of Duty game in the past decade-plus, you'll have interacted with Houston's work: he was a central creative force behind the writing for Treyarch's campaign modes since 2006 (with Call of Duty 3) and the main writer for the Zombies mode since 2008 (with Call of Duty: World at War). Alongside Jimmy Zielinski, Jason Blundell, and Kevin Drew, Houston was an integral part of the evolution of the Zombies pillar of Call of Duty, and shaped it into the series-defining thing it is today. There has been a fair amount of community support for Houston since he declared the news yesterday; he was a popular dev, and a lot of the Zombies-specific fan communities online hold a lot of respect for him.

In a recent development, "Craig is a great guy," notes one user on Reddit. "You can tell how much he loves the story/characters he writes just by how excited he is when he talks about them in promo material.".

Sources indicate that "You're a Legend Craig, it was an honor to work with you," notes ex-Treyarch vet, Tony Flame, in a reply to Houston's X post. "You created a truly special experience that will live on in the kinds of millions fans. Wishing you the best [...].".

From all of us here at Eurogamer, and myself personally - who really admires the character-work and emergent storytelling present in the Xbox 360-era Call of Duty games, specifically - we wish you the best and good luck with the future, Craig.

Xbox hardware sales were up 42% in October in the U.S. year-over-year. It's been donkeys since we've seen positive news attached to this level of stonks coming out of Microsoft, so we'll take it!

According to recent reports, the figures were shared in a monthly report from the statistical boffins over at Circana. Mat Piscatella revealed that US hardware spending was up by 2% compared to October last year. PlayStation 5 sales grew by 20%, Switch 2 dropped 11%, and Xbox Series surged by 42%. Phwoar!

However, Piscatella made sure to point out that "higher pricing was the primary driver of dollar sales growth" for Xbox Series, as "XBS unit sales grew by 10%" whilst the average selling price also bumped up by 29%.

Xbox's planned hardware price increase came into effect back in August, but according to Circana, Gears of War: E-Day and GTA 6 "may have provided at least a temporary reprieve" for the console's sales figures.

"It’s no secret that Xbox Series hardware sales have struggled in recent years. Gears and GTA may have provided at least a temporary reprieve.".

Recent findings suggest that gears of War: E-Day appears to be something of a console mover, and I'd wager help from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 played a part too. Microsoft has claimed the top two spots in Circana's projected best-selling video games chart for October 2026, taking both physical and digital dollar sales into consideration.

Modern Warfare 4 was the best-selling game of October, which Piscatella also noted makes it the "19th consecutive year that a Call of Duty franchise release has been the best-selling game of its debut month".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A new Cyberpunk 2077 mod has overhauled Night City's rain, swapping the game's flat wet weather effects for individual 3D drops and adding lightning storms.

Recent findings suggest that as spotted by DSOGaming, modder CyanideX's mod, Torrent, gives each raindrop its own size and falling speed. The drops also react to the player's movement, so they stream towards the windscreen when you're driving fast. If you find the wind has picked up, blustery weather can also push them sideways, too.

It has been revealed that the rain also catches the light from street lamps, neon signs, car headlights, and taillights, and won't fall through roofs or inside buildings. Drops splash on the ground, heavy rain leaves mist in the distance, and cars throw up spray from their tyres on wet roads.

The mod complements this with a new lightning system, with branching bolts that flash and flicker before fading, and that can arrive in bursts during heavier storms.

If you like a little lightning, the frequency of bolts can be adjusted across 10 levels, and with the AudioXL mod installed, thunder follows each strike, timed to how far away it landed.

For players sensitive to flashing lights, a Reduce Flashes option dims the lightning, replaces its flicker with a single slow glow, and halves the number of strikes.

Torrent supports Nova City 2 and other weather mods, and adds extra storm effects for Nova City 2 players, including mist that rolls through the streets with the wind. It’s available now on Nexus Mods.

In a recent development, mucky and disreputable kiosk game Probably Stolen – Cyberpunk Shopkeeper Sim is getting three major updates over the next few months that add extra starting scenarios, building on the existing wealth of goods, materials, vocations and techs. Those starting scenarios range from peddling human meat to running the finest cyber-frappucino stall this side of Tannhäuser Gate. There are no hard release dates, and the contents of each upgrade may alter, but developers Questing Goose Studio have shared some rough timeframes.

Coming up in mid-December, there's the Junker starting scenario, which I assume is all about trading scrap, rather than being a Prussian nobleman. You'll get a bespoke perk, upcoming items, and the ability to hire, equip and send scavs on expeditions. This upgrade will also include some minor expansions for the Fence and Gunsmith vocations – the latter will be able to flog or otherwise make use of shotgun shells, 25mm grenade rounds and a tier 3 handmade SMG, alongside new armour.

Late January is when you'll "very likely" get the chance to be an Organ Dealer, care of the second major upgrade. "Players will start by buying different organs and fulfilling specific requests, and will later be able to grow or print organs," a Steam blog explains. You'll also be able to filter blood and remove diseases, with different blood types having different value modifiers. How will you get your hands on organs? By sending horrible black market thugs on foraging "expeditions".

Sources indicate that last but not least, the planned April patch will add the Street Food Vendor starting scenario. This lets you weave a livelihood around choice beverages and edibles from a range of cultures, supported by updates to the game's Aquaculture and Hydroponics tech. Sounds a lot cheerier than the organ trading racket, but then again, Probably Stolen will doubtless find a way to make it utterly grim. Guests at Sweeney's Cantina know better than to ask what our frappucinos are made of.

According to recent reports, are you playing Probably Stolen? It's been doing better than expected. I was keen on the demo, but my attention was lured away by a truly upsetting game about dogpeople in caves.

Police have arrested a suspect after a drive-by shooting at an office campus in Tustin, California, which is home to Xbox-owned studio inXile Entertainment.

According to Aftermath, officers responded to reports of a drive-by shooting at Flight at Tustin Legacy, a campus that houses inXile and other businesses, on 11th November.

Sources indicate that "Located multiple shell casings. Nobody was hurt," Tustin Police Sergeant Christopher Peterson told the outlet. "Processed the crime scene, and then sometime [Friday] morning, a little before 11 [AM], they took a suspect into custody. And the investigation is still kind of ongoing as to where and why.".

"We're relieved that no one was hurt at our inXile office," an inXile spokesperson mentioned. "Our focus is on supporting our team, and we are working closely with law enforcement as they investigate.".

Police have not given a motive, and the suspect has not been named.

InXile is the studio behind the Wasteland series, and is presently working on Clockwork Revolution.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, knights of the Old Republic is my favorite RPG of all time, and a key reason why my love of video games developed as deeply as it did.
  • "I think it would be really weird to do if I hadn't worked on the first one," Hudson admits in an interview for The Fourth Curtain podcast.
  • According to recent reports, hudson states that experience "helps," because the studio knows "why we did things the way we did.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, knights of the Old Republic is my favorite RPG of all time, and a key reason why my love of video games developed as deeply as it did. My hopes for Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic, a spiritual successor to BioWare's classic, are sky-high, and expectations from the broader community are similarly intense. Director Casey Hudson isn't too worried about that pressure, though – after all, he and much of the team at Arcanaut Studios made the original KOTOR and the Mass Effect trilogy.

"I think it would be really weird to do if I hadn't worked on the first one," Hudson admits in an interview for The Fourth Curtain podcast. "It would feel really strange. But I think, for us, we've got folks on the team who worked on that game and have worked on all the Mass Effect games since and other BioWare stuff.".

According to recent reports, hudson states that experience "helps," because the studio knows "why we did things the way we did. We're not trying to fill someone else's shoes, despite the expectations being really high.".

It has been revealed that we still know very little about Fate of the Old Republic, other than the fact that it's a spiritual successor to KOTOR. What kind of gameplay systems will it build on? I can't imagine KOTOR's creaky D&D 3.5-based mechanics are going to make a comeback. What kind of story will it tell? It's going to have to be something all-new, with the entire Star Wars universe having been rebooted since KOTOR was new.

"The thing that supersedes everything is our passion and excitement for doing something amazing," Hudson claims. "That has to outshine everything else, because you can't really know how to answer pressure, and it's hard to even really understand what other people want to play. But if you're so excited about making something that people are going to love, you're just passionate about it being amazing, that leads you to where you want to go.".

That's maybe an obvious answer, but I appreciate that it's the one Hudson is providing. No latest game can possibly live up to my nostalgic memories of BioWare's Star Wars RPG, and what I really want is a new game created by a team of people who are excited about what they're making. If it can tap into my old love for KOTOR, that's just icing on the cake.

Star Wars: Fate of the Old Republic director Casey Hudson says there'll be "newly introduced announcements" about the KOTOR successor next year.

Sources indicate that if you want to play GTA 6 natively on any console right now, you can only do so on Xbox Series X, Xbox Series S or PS5. However, if you're willing to use the cloud, it's possible to play the game on Xbox One.

To do this, you have to buy the game on the Xbox Store first, and then acquire Xbox Cloud Gaming time via one of two means - you either purchase time on the Xbox Store, or you get a subscription to Xbox Game Pass that includes a certain amount of time per-tier (and you can top it up later if you need to).

Here's the breakdown for all of those:.

In a recent development, there is also the option to play "free with ads" using Xbox Cloud Gaming, but we haven't verified that it works with GTA 6 yet (although there's seemingly no reason why it wouldn't), and it only gives you 30 minutes of game time before it kicks you off. Some of GTA 6's missions can last longer than 30 minutes, so that's not really ideal.

Anyway, while we're still in the process of dusting off our Xbox One consoles and trying GTA 6 on there for ourselves, we thought we'd first share some impressions from Xbox fans across the web on what it's been like for them so far.

Let's take a look at what some Xbox One owners are saying about it:.

Overall, it seems like most people are enjoying their time with GTA 6 on Xbox One so far, although that's not to say there haven't been complications in some cases. The biggest complaints seem to be that some players think it looks "blurry" (while others don't really see a problem), and there are also a small number of reports that it appears to disconnect for no reason sometimes.

There's also a bit of worry that the servers might not be able to handle the load during "peak" hours, and considering we're only on the first day of GTA 6's official launch, it's hard to say how things are going to go in that regard.

Meanwhile, every other version of Xbox Cloud Gaming officially runs at up to 1080p and 12mbps bitrate.

If you want any further feedback about playing GTA 6 on the Xbox One, we'll aim to get some "hands on" impressions to you ASAP. Based on these initial day one impressions though, it seems to be working fairly well right now.

Keep in mind that you obviously need a strong and consistent internet connection in order to play games via Xbox Cloud Gaming, otherwise you may experience heavy lag, disconnects and all sorts of other problems.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that A lot of Survivor fans are still in their feels about the coin flip, and let the record show, fan favorite and multi-time player Kelley Wentworth is among the frustrated.
  • During her extended rant, Wentworth ran down a laundry list of problems.
  • Recent findings suggest that I don’t like the coin flip.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A lot of Survivor fans are still in their feels about the coin flip, and let the record show, fan favorite and multi-time player Kelley Wentworth is among the frustrated. She dropped a video yesterday going off about the game mechanic and talking through in very specific detail exactly why she wants it gone.

During her extended rant, Wentworth ran down a laundry list of problems. She brought up how Lewis apparently won the coin toss but then was told it didn’t count because it landed outside the little circular mat host Jeff Probst had put down. She brought up how every single fan with any time awareness knew he was going to lose the coin flip because there wasn’t enough time left in the episode to vote. And more broadly, she brought up the fact that we’re never going to be able to recreate the special circumstances of the original coin flip with Rick Devens on 50, so what’s the point in trying. You can read her blunt words about that below….

Recent findings suggest that I don’t like the coin flip. I don’t like it. We should have left that in season 50 along with Mr. Beast and Rick Devens flipping it. This coin flip was only fun in 50 because of all the circumstances, because it was Mr. Beast and it was so ridiculous, because it was Rick and he was on the bottom and he was so excited about doing it and it actually worked. Yes, this is a very results based twist, but bringing this back in 51 and now we’re carrying it into other seasons? No. This did not hit the same. I don’t like it. I don’t care about the increased prize money. This was just depressing.

Sources indicate that she’s obviously right. I wasn’t a huge fan of the coin flip on 50. I could see where the show was coming from though because it felt like a grandiose, over the top one-off moment that matched a milestone season and a fun, reckless player always willing to gamble. The circumstances just worked, even if it’s not a game mechanic I personally would have designed.

In a recent development, this season, however, it felt really forced and out of place. We’ve been getting banger tribal council after banger tribal council with some of the most interesting votes in the history of the show. What most of us wanted, as fans, was just to watch the players do that again, but instead, we lost one of the season’s most entertaining characters on a freakin’ coin flip. As Wentworth put it, it’s just depressing.

You can watch her full rant in all its glory below….

A post shared by kelleywentworth (@kelleywentworth).

In a recent development, survivor has already declared that the coin flip is coming back for future seasons. During Survivor 52, one player will flip for the chance to push the prize pot to three million dollars. I hope it hits, and then I hope the producers take a look at the coin flip and its future in the game.

Sources indicate that like Wentworth, I’d personally like to see it removed, but if the show is going to keep it, they should at least experiment with a different structure and/ or different rules. Maybe one player can decide at any point after jury to flip it, and they just announce it at tribal. Maybe all the players vote and then someone decides whether they want to negate it. Maybe it’s a one-time option the players are allowed to pass on. Maybe a player wins an advantage and they personally get to decide whether to flip it or not flip it.

Your Daily Blend of Entertainment News.

Industry observers note that regardless, I’m going to stay positive on Survivor 51. Yes, the coin flip was a big bummer. Yes, it was devastating to lose Lewis, but even so, this is the best season we’ve gotten in a long time. The cast is half crazies and half schemers, and there are already like five moments that will be referenced for years to come, including Brady’s chopped finger, the most embarrassing quit in show history, Kilby standing on business and the blindside of poor Pantsless Patt. Fingers crossed the rest of the season gives us a few more and in doing so, solidifies its place as an all-time great season.

EA hires another former Call of Duty boss to take the lead on all Battlefield Studios' projects
